title.narrative: HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis Sustaining collaboration to strengthen TB/HIV services - Guyana (01-Jan-2025-31-Dec-2027)

description.narrative: Guyana, TB/HIV, Ministry of Health of the Co-operative Republic of Guyana (MOH)This program has the following goals: To reduce stigma and discrimination, new HIV infections, and AIDS-related deaths, and tackle critical enablers for ending AIDS in Guyana, promote people-centred, gender-sensitive and rights-based enabling environments and systems, in order to give an effective and sustainable response to HIV and TB, by, (i) closing the gap in the progress towards the 95-95-95 targets: increase early HIV detection, ensure a rapid scale up of ART and improve HIV care quality, by promoting innovative prevention interventions, and (ii) scaling up the access to an effective up-to-date TB diagnosis, treatment and prevention (with special attention to vulnerbale population,KPs). The objectives of this program are: Increase early HIV detection, scale up ART and improve HIV care quality, by promoting innovative testing approaches, ensuring access to quality ART, implementing differentiated people-centered models of HIV treatment and care/ ART, and addressing the weak linkages in the HIV care continuum. Prevent HIV transmission, by expanding the coverage of innovative prevention interventions among key populations, integrate health service platforms at community level, and remove the dichotomy between HIV prevention and HIV care service continuums. Ensure universal access to timely and quality diagnosis and detection of TB (with emphasis on RR/MDR-TB) - by rolling out rapid molecular diagnostic testing, improving the quality and coverage of DST, and promoting active targeted case finding (screening for TB in high risk groups mainly). Improve the treatment outcomes of DR-TB patients by implementing modified shorter treatment regimens and scaling-up people-centred approaches, comprehensive patient support and follow up activities. Reduce TB transmission by scaling up effective preventive treatment and improving infection control. Health system strengthening. Remove human rights and gender barriers and achieve zero discrimination
